label: ex:hopf-diquark-crossing-energy
title: Hopf crossing energy of a diquark
html:
Example. Hopf crossing energy of a diquark

Crossing energy. The Hopf link \mathcal{L}_H = T_{2,2} has braid word \sigma_1^2 with 2 crossings. For a diquark composed of quarks with crossing orientations \epsilon_i, \epsilon_j \in \{+1, -1\}, the Hopf crossing energy is:

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(D_{ij}^{[ab]})
  = 
  \epsilon_i \cdot q^{\epsilon_i}
  + 
  \epsilon_j \cdot q^{\epsilon_j}
  + 
  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathcal{L}_H),

where \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathcal{L}_H) provides the linking contribution. An attractive (binding) diquark requires \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}} < 0.
